artifact_schema.description: The discrete logarithm, as 64 lowercase hex characters.

k.description: k with k*G = Q, in [1, n), zero-padded to exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.

statement: A worked ECDLP demonstration, and the smallest rung of the ladder: find k with k*G = Q on the 45-bit prime-order curve pinned in the checker. Baby-step giant-step needs about 2^22 group operations -- around twenty seconds of Python. THE ANSWER SHIPS WITH THIS EXAMPLE, in examples/ecdlp/artifact.json, so this is a demonstration rather than an open bounty: run `proofwork try` against it and watch a claim settle end to end. It mints nothing for a second submitter, because a duplicate verifies fine and earns zero. The instance is nothing-up-my-sleeve -- prime, curve, G and Q are all SHA-256 outputs of the public seed in the checker, re-derivable with `examples/certicom-ecdlp/tools/nums.py verify`. It replaced a secp256k1 instance whose scalar was confined to a one-bit window, which meant its author had chosen and therefore knew the answer while presenting it as an open bounty. For objectives nobody has solved, see examples/certicom-ecdlp/.
